properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Dependency inventory (updated): MD5 ships in FOUR toolchains of this build — md5@2.3.0 in browsertests, wallet_web and wallet_admin_portal pnpm lockfiles (transitive), plus the md-5 crate in wallet_core's Cargo.lock. The browsertests/wallet_core sites were judged from their packages; the wallet_web and wallet_admin_portal lockfile hits are the same package reached by different manifests.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: sha1@0.10.6 resolved in the wallet_core workspace lockfile — the build ships a SHA-1 implementation. Whether application code or a transitive dependency drives it is a separate question; this is the dependency-inventory entry for it.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: AES-CMAC is a load-bearing MAC in wallet_core: lib/crypto uses the cmac 0.7.2 crate as the S2V component of its AES-SIV implementation (aes_siv.rs), and lib/hsm computes CMAC on HSM-held AES keys (Mechanism::AesCMac, AesKeyUsage::Cmac) for the wallet_provider message-signing path. CMAC is symmetric-key cryptography, quantum-safe in transit but bound to AES key sizes; sites in hsm/test.rs and the aes_siv test helper exercise the same live path.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: RSA-SHA256 (RS256) is the JOSE signing algorithm across the OAuth/OIDC layer: the mock advertises RS256 for id_token signing (mock.rs:39), userinfo.rs builds/validates RS256-signed JWTs (414/423/430/437), and openid4vc client_auth.rs negotiates/checks RS256 as the client-authentication JWS algorithm (353/358/379/384). Shor-vulnerable signature scheme; migration ML-DSA-65 or hybrid. Changeable here.

components.name: Java JSSE sessions on default settings (at least JDK 21)

Quantum-unsafe (Shor) with deadline-class urgency for signatures;

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: AES-CCM/SIV as implemented by lib/crypto's aes_siv.rs: an AES-SIV (RFC 5297) deterministic AEAD built on AES-256-CMAC (see also ALG-f6a9ef33), used to protect wallet_provider signed-account flows; the hsm/test.rs sites exercise the HSM-backed variant. Symmetric, quantum-safe against harvest-now (Grover only halves key strength from 256 to 128 bits), so this is an inventory-keep, not a PQ urgency; the [A-] rating reflects AES key-size context rather than a migration deadline.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: HMAC-SHA-256 as the GBA hc-converter's MAC: preloaded hmac_key used to MAC GBA request/response payloads (gba/encryption.rs, client.rs) and to hash account names for lookup (name_to_encoded_hash), plus HSM-side HMAC-SHA-256 in lib/hsm/src/model. Symmetric MAC — quantum-safe; the GBA converter is a service tool for converting government brokered-authentication secrets. Changeable here.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: sha2@0.10.9 resolved in the wallet_core workspace lockfile — the SHA-2 crate backing hashes, HMAC-SHA-256 and HKDF-SHA-256 throughout wallet_core. Dependency-inventory entry; the hash itself is quantum-resistant for preimage/collision purposes at 256 bits.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: The AES-256 key-size view of the wallet's symmetric cryptography: Aes256Gcm in the GBA hc-converter, mdoc disclosure sessions, wallet storage key files and the mock hw_keystore, plus Cmac::<Aes256> and Ctr128BE::<Aes256> inside lib/crypto's AES-SIV implementation. Largely the same call sites as the AES-GCM object (ALG-f61ec50f) plus the AES-SIV CMAC/CTR core; kept separate because it captures the 256-bit key size dimension. Grover leaves a 128-bit margin — quantum-safe, no migration needed.
